review_candidates.title: Tier 2 Infrastructure & Network Engineer - Prince George, BC
review_candidates.description: About CORE Core Network Solutions Inc. is a Canadian managed IT services and network infrastructure company with more than 23 years of operation, serving over 150 clients across Western Canada from our head office in St. Albert, Alberta and our regional office in Prince George, British Columbia. We design, deploy and manage network, security and infrastructure environments for municipalities, health authorities and private-sector organizations — clients who expect their infrastructure to simply work, and who count on us when it doesn’t. Position Summary We are looking for a Tier 2 Infrastructure & Network Engineer to take a lead role in the design, deployment and ongoing operation of client network, virtualization and security environments. This is a hands-on senior role: you will own project delivery from design through cutover, act as the top escalation point for complex technical issues, and travel to client sites across Western Canada to deliver network implementations. The successful candidate is a broad, senior generalist — strong in enterprise networking, comfortable at a Linux command line, fluent in containerized and virtualized workloads, and confident configuring next-generation firewalls and web application firewalls. Key Responsibilities Network Implementation & Engineering •     Design, configure and deploy enterprise LAN, WAN, SD-WAN and wireless environments for client sites, including switching, routing, VLAN architecture and QoS. •     Lead network implementation projects end to end: requirements gathering, design documentation, bill of materials, staging and configuration, on-site installation, cutover and post-deployment validation. •     Configure and maintain routing and switching platforms across CORE’s core vendor lines, including Fortinet, Juniper, HPE, Arista and Check Point. •     Plan and execute network migrations and refreshes with minimal client disruption, including after-hours cutover windows. •     Implement and troubleshoot site-to-site and remote access VPN, including IPsec, IKEv2 and SSL VPN. •     Produce and maintain accurate network documentation: topology diagrams, IP schemas, configuration standards and as-built records. Linux Administration •     Deploy, harden, patch and administer Linux servers (Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL-family) in client and internal environments. •     Manage core Linux services including DNS, DHCP, NTP, SSH, web and reverse-proxy services, certificate management and log forwarding. •     Write and maintain shell scripts and lightweight automation to standardize repetitive administrative tasks. •     Perform Linux-level performance analysis and root cause investigation using standard diagnostic tooling. •     Apply security hardening baselines, manage user and privilege models, and support client audit and compliance requirements. Container & Docker Administration •     Deploy, configure and maintain Docker hosts and containerized workloads supporting client and internal services. •     Build and maintain container images, Docker Compose stacks, persistent storage and container networking. •     Monitor container health, resource consumption and logging; manage lifecycle, updates and image hygiene. •     Apply container security practices including image provenance, least-privilege runtime configuration and registry management. Cybersecurity — NGFW and WAF •     Deploy, configure and manage next-generation firewalls, including policy design, application control, IPS/IDS, URL filtering, TLS inspection and threat prevention profiles. •     Deploy and tune web application firewalls, including rule sets, policy exceptions, false-positive tuning and protection of published client applications. •     Implement network segmentation and zero-trust-aligned access policies across client environments. •     Support CORE’s CNSsecure security offerings and integrate deployed controls with client monitoring and reporting. •     Investigate security events, analyze firewall and system logs, and produce clear post-incident findings for clients. •     Stay current with emerging threats, vendor advisories and firmware and security patching cycles across managed platforms. Hypervisor Deployment & Management •     Design, deploy and manage virtualization platforms including Proxmox VE, Microsoft Hyper-V and Morpheus. •     Build and maintain clustered hypervisor environments including shared storage, high availability and live migration. •     Manage virtual machine lifecycle: provisioning, templating, resource allocation, snapshots and capacity planning. •     Configure virtual networking, distributed switching and hypervisor-level segmentation. •     Integrate virtualization platforms with backup and recovery tooling, and regularly validate restore capability. •     Perform hypervisor upgrades, patching and migrations between platforms. Project Travel & On-Site Delivery •     Travel to client sites across Alberta, British Columbia and Western Canada to deliver network and infrastructure implementations — approximately 25% of working time, typically in multi-day blocks scheduled in advance. •     Perform physical installation work: rack and stack, structured cabling termination and dressing, device mounting, labelling and equipment decommissioning. Troubleshooting & Analysis •     Serve as the senior escalation point for complex, cross-domain issues spanning network, server, virtualization and security layers. •     Apply a structured diagnostic method — reproduce, isolate the fault domain, test hypotheses, confirm root cause, remediate — rather than trial-and-error changes. •     Use packet capture and protocol analysis, log correlation and performance monitoring tooling to resolve issues others could not. •     Document root cause analyses and feed findings back into standards, monitoring and preventative maintenance. •     Mentor intermediate and junior technical staff in diagnostic technique and escalation discipline. Client Service & Managed Services Delivery •     Meet service level commitments and communicate proactively when timelines or scope change. •     Communicate directly with client technical and non-technical stakeholders •     Maintain client documentation to CORE standards •     Contribute to scoping, estimating and technical review of proposals and statements of work. •     Participate in the on-call rotation and after-hours maintenance windows as scheduled. Qualifications Required •     6–10+ years of progressive experience in network and infrastructure engineering, ideally including time with a managed services provider, VAR or multi-client consulting firm. •     Demonstrated experience leading network implementation projects end to end, on client sites. •     Strong hands-on enterprise routing and switching expertise, including VLANs, spanning tree, dynamic routing protocols and WAN/SD-WAN technologies. •     Solid Linux administration skills at the command line, including services, scripting, hardening and diagnostics. •     Practical Docker and container administration experience in a production context. •     Hands-on next-generation firewall experience — policy design, threat prevention, VPN and troubleshooting — plus working knowledge of web application firewalls. •     Hypervisor deployment and management experience with at least two of Proxmox VE, Hyper-V or Morpheus, and the capacity to become proficient in all three. •     Excellent troubleshooting and analytical ability across multiple technology layers. •     Strong written and verbal communication in English, including client-facing documentation. •     Valid Class 5 driver’s licence and a reliable vehicle for local and regional travel. •     Ability to pass criminal record and security clearance checks required by public-sector and health-sector clients. •     Legally entitled to work in Canada. Preferred •     Experience serving Canadian public-sector or health-sector clients (municipal, county, health authority). •     Familiarity with CORE’s primary vendor lines: Check Point, Fortinet, Juniper, HPE, Arista, Lenovo and Microsoft. •     Backup and disaster recovery experience, particularly where Canadian data residency is required. •     Infrastructure-as-code, configuration management or CI/CD exposure (Ansible, Terraform, Git-based workflows). •     Monitoring and observability tooling experience. •     Microsoft 365 and Entra ID / Active Directory administration. •     Experience mentoring or leading a small technical team. Certifications Certifications are valued, but demonstrated capability matters more. Any of the following are considered assets, and CORE supports certification pursuit for the right candidate. •     Security: Check Point CCSA / CCSE, Fortinet NSE 4–7, CompTIA Security+, SSCP •     Networking: Juniper JNCIA / JNCIS, JNCIP, JNCIE,Cisco CCNA / CCNP, CCIE, HPE Aruba ACSA / ACSP •     Linux: LPIC-1 / LPIC-2, Red Hat RHCSA / RHCE, CompTIA Linux+ •     Virtualization: Proxmox VE certification, Microsoft AZ-800 / AZ-801, VMware VCP •     Containers: Docker Certified Associate, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) Working Conditions •     Based at CORE’s Prince George, BC office, with a mix of office, client-site and remote work. •     Approximately 25% travel, primarily within Alberta and British Columbia, including occasional overnight and multi-day trips to rural and remote client sites. Travel is scheduled in advance wherever possible. •     Scheduled after-hours and weekend maintenance windows are a normal part of infrastructure cutover work. •     Participation in an on-call rotation. •     Physical requirements include lifting and positioning equipment up to approximately 50 lbs, working in server rooms and equipment closets. Core Network Solutions Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to providing accommodation for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process — please let us know if you require accommodation.

This role supports business operations by managing servers, networks, cloud platforms, cybersecurity initiatives, enterprise applications, and end-user technology. The IT Systems Administrator works closely with the IT Director and business stakeholders to ensure reliable system performance, data security, and exceptional technical support while driving continuous technology improvements across the organization. Draft scripts and/or deploy programs to assist with automation, provisioning, and/or telemetry, and to ensure integrity of resources to dependent systems. Log and manage incidents in ticketing systems while maintaining technical documentation, including diagrams and standard operating procedures. review_candidates.title: Systems Consultant
review_candidates.description: About CCT Founded in 2012, CCT pioneered revenue audit automation for land-based casinos, eliminating manual reconciliation and improving financial visibility. Our flagship platform, Casino Insight, provides a detailed, audit-ready view of cash transactions across the casino floor — supporting compliance, operational efficiency, and fraud prevention. Today CCT serves over 300 casinos across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. The Role Systems Consultants build and maintain the infrastructure that Casino Insight runs on. When a casino buys CCT, a Systems Consultant stands up the environment: Windows and SQL Server, the application and message-queue tiers, remote access, and the linkedserver connections that pull data out of the property's slot, table, cage, and sportsbook systems. After go-live, the same Systems Consultant owns that environment's health and is the escalation point when something breaks. It is a genuine consulting role. Most client IT departments are small, and many have never integrated a system like ours. You are the expert in the room — advising on architecture, negotiating firewall and access changes, and enabling the client's team to support their side of the deployment after handoff. You do this work from our Tulsa office, not from the casino floor. Nearly every environment build, upgrade, and troubleshooting session happens remotely over screen shares with client IT, so travel is under 10% — occasional go-live support, a client visit, or an industry event. Sitting with the team matters early on: this is a role you learn by overhearing how the person next to you talks a client's network admin through a firewall change. Systems Consultants who are established in the role have the opportunity to move to a hybrid schedule. What You'll Actually Do Build client environments (largest share of the role) Stand up application and database servers for new Insight Cash and Insight Analytics implementations — Windows Server, IIS, MS SQL Server, TLS certificates, service accounts, scheduled jobs Deploy and configure CCT's Data Bridge tier for single-site and multi-property clients Configure linked servers and third-party data connections across MSSQL, Oracle, AS400/DB2, and PostgreSQL — slot systems, ticketing, kiosks and recyclers, table games, sportsbook Set up employee Active Directory sync, report distribution, backups Cove, and training-environment refreshes from production Own the network and access layer Work with client IT to troubleshoot network issues between servers and workstations Establish AWS site-to-site VPN tunnels against client firewalls FortiGate, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, pfSense, and others). If you've done this before, great — if you haven't, we'll teach you. Solid TCP/IP fundamentals matter more here than prior AWS experience Configure and maintain SecureLink remote access, including gatekeeper setup and audit review Support on-prem to AWS replication for hybrid client architectures Run upgrades and keep environments healthy Execute CAS push upgrades and MQ upgrades across the client base Diagnose and resolve escalated production issues — service failures, blocked ports, failed jobs, disk and performance problems, broken integrations Monitor environment health and patch levels; act on alerts before clients notice Consult and document Lead client IT kickoff calls: walk their team through requirements, architecture, and their responsibilities Produce clear technical documentation — configuration guides, environment records in Passportal, and knowledge-base articles the rest of the team relies on Support internal CCT IT and end-user requests as part of a shared rotation Tools you'll use: MS SQL Server / SSMS, Windows Server, Hyper-V, IIS, Active Directory, AWS VPC, VPN, EC2, S3, IAM, CloudWatch), SecureLink, Passportal, N Central, SentinelOne, Cove, Freshdesk, Mavenlink, Notion, GitHub, Slack. What Success Looks Like First 30 days: Local and lab environments built; oriented on the CCT stack; handling internal IT and enablement tickets with review First 60 days: Completing a full server environment build in lab independently; running Data Bridge deployments and upgrades in client environments with light supervision First 90 days: Owning a client environment build end-to-end, leading a client IT kickoff call, and handling standard support tickets without review New Systems Consultants work through a structured 90-day plan with a defined milestone checklist, shadowing time with each member of the team, and a specialty track chosen with your manager (networking, database, integrations, or internal IT. How We Expect You To Think This is the part of the job we care most about, and it's the part that's hardest to teach. Our documentation is good, and you will use it. However, a runbook cannot tell you why step 6 exists, what it assumes about the client's network, or what to do when the environment in front of you doesn't match the one the runbook was written against. Working through the steps without understanding the mechanism behind them is how a build passes every checkbox and still fails at go-live. What that looks like day to day: Understand the why before the how. You should be able to explain what a linked server actually does, why a VPN tunnel needs matching phase-2 selectors, or why a service account failed after a password policy change — not just recall the fix that worked last time. Diagnose, don't guess. Read the error. Check the log. Form a hypothesis, test the one thing that would disprove it, and narrow from there. Restarting services and re-running the installer until something changes is not troubleshooting. Know when you're outside what you understand. Being unsure is fine and expected — this stack is deep. Pretending otherwise in front of a client's IT director is not. Ask, escalate, or go read, then come back with an answer you can defend. Improve the process you inherited. When you find a gap, an undocumented step, or a step that exists only because someone once did it that way, say so and fix it. We would rather hear "this instruction is wrong and here's why" than watch it get followed for another two years. Be genuinely curious. The people who do well here take apart systems they've never seen because they want to know how they work, not because a ticket forced them to. Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in a technical field (Computer Science, MIS, Computer Engineering, etc.), or equivalent practical experience Hands-on proficiency with MS SQL Server (backup/restore, scheduled jobs, linked servers, permissions), Windows Server, Active Directory, and IIS Working knowledge of TCP/IP networking — firewalls, NAT, VPN concepts, DNS, certificates, port troubleshooting Excellent written and verbal communication; able to explain a technical requirement to a client's IT director and to write documentation someone else can follow Demonstrated troubleshooting discipline — a structured method for isolating a problem, and the ability to walk us through the reasoning behind a hard issue you solved, not just the outcome (see "How We Expect You to Think") Comfortable owning multiple client projects at once and driving them to a deadline without being managed day to day Ability to pass stringent background investigations and obtain gaming licensure/registration where required by client jurisdictions Preferred 3+ years in systems administration, infrastructure engineering, implementation consulting, or a comparable technical role AWS experience, especially VPC networking and site-to-site VPN — a real advantage, but something we're prepared to train Virtualization (Hyper-V, VMware) and cloud or hybrid infrastructure Exposure to Oracle, DB2/AS400, or PostgreSQL Scripting for automation (PowerShell, T SQL) Gaming, hospitality, or another regulated industry Relevant certifications (AWS, Microsoft, CompTIA Network+/Security+) Working Conditions Our team works on-site in the Tulsa, OK office, collaborating daily with client IT over calls and shared remote sessions. Hybrid flexibility opens up once you're established in the role Travel under 10% Casinos operate 24/7, so cutovers, upgrades, and go-lives are occasionally scheduled outside standard hours or on weekends. This is planned in advance, not routine On-call duty rotates weekly among the SC team, covering escalated production issues Work Authorization This position is not eligible for employer-sponsored work authorization or visa sponsorship (including initial, transfer, or extension). Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and remain authorized for the duration of employment without the need for sponsorship. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

review_candidates.description: About Allia Health Group Allia Health Group is a fast-growing digital health system revolutionizing metabolic, hormonal, and longevity care. Allia is building the future of healthcare by being clinician-first and patient-centered. We are innovative, empathetic, and accessible to our patients, combining cutting-edge tools with human-centered care to make high-quality longevity and wellness solutions affordable and available to more people. Why join us? At Allia Health Group, you're part of something bigger — helping shape a mission-driven enterprise that's scaling rapidly, solving real problems in healthcare inefficiencies, and making a tangible difference in people's lives every day. Position Summary Own the on-premise network and its security at the Southend Pharmacy compounding facility and across the infrastructure supporting our brands, working with the CTO organization’s cloud security team where site infrastructure meets cloud workloads. Beyond keeping things connected, this role builds the logging, alerting, and monitoring layer that lets us see security and availability events, which is our biggest blind spot today. Escalation and change approval run through the IT Operations Lead. Identity-integrated network access is coordinated with the Systems Administrator. Key Responsibilities Network Segmentation: Design and maintain zones that separate compounding production systems, PHI-bearing workstations, clinical devices, administrative users, and guest or BYOD traffic, which the 2026 HIPAA Security Rule expects. Firewall & Perimeter Management: Own the firewall rule lifecycle, including documented periodic review, change approval, and elimination of undocumented or overly permissive rules. Logging Architecture: Deploy and operate centralized log collection spanning firewalls, switches, wireless, servers, endpoints, and pharmacy production systems, with retention configured to the standard set by the compliance program. Alerting & Detection: Build tuned alert rules with clear severity tiers routed to a named responder. The goal is a manageable number of alerts that are worth acting on. Proactive Monitoring: Track throughput, latency, packet loss, and capacity on production-critical paths, watching trends so problems surface before they turn into outages. Site Connectivity & Redundancy: Manage carrier circuits and redundant paths for the pharmacy and supporting sites, and test failover on a schedule so we know it works. Wireless Infrastructure: Deploy enterprise wireless with certificate-based authentication and separate production, corporate, and guest SSIDs, tuned for the density of scanners and mobile devices on the production floor. Secure Remote Access: Administer VPN and Zero Trust network access for remote staff and offshore contractors, in coordination with the Systems Administrator (Identity & IAM). Vulnerability Management: Run regular scans of network-attached infrastructure and track fixes to closure, documenting risk acceptance where a fix is deferred. Technical Incident Response: Lead the technical side of security incidents, covering detection, triage, containment, eradication, and the write-up afterward. Pre-Authorized Containment: Act immediately on lower-severity events such as isolating an endpoint, disabling an account, or blocking an address, and notify afterward. Escalate to the IT Operations Lead when there is suspected PHI exposure, when an action would affect compounding production, or when an incident stays open past its severity clock. Configuration & Change Control: Version all network configurations, keep topology documentation current, and produce evidence supporting SOC 2 change-management controls. Circuit & Vendor Governance: Hold carriers and hardware vendors accountable to contracted service levels, and plan end-of-life refresh before equipment becomes an availability risk. Site Coverage Backup: Provide on-site coverage for the IT Support Specialist during absences or overlapping production incidents, following documented runbook procedures only. This role does not own tickets or work the standard support queue. Coverage: Standard hours are 08:00 to 17:00 CST, Monday through Friday, with participation in an on-call rotation for production-critical and security events outside those hours. IT Network Specialist — Qualifications Education Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, network engineering, or a related field preferred. Equivalent hands-on experience is accepted in place of a degree. Required Certifications CCNA, or equivalent vendor certification for comparable platforms (JNCIA, Aruba ACSA, Fortinet FCP), or demonstrated equivalent skill CompTIA Security+, or equivalent security fundamentals credential Preferred Certifications Firewall certification for Palo Alto PCNSA/PCNSE, Fortinet NSE, Cisco Firepower CWNA (Certified Wireless Network Administrator) Cisco CyberOps Associate, GIAC GCIH, or comparable incident response training Required Experience 5-8 years in network administration or network engineering At least 2 years owning a production network environment, including change decisions and escalation, rather than working assigned tickets within someone else's design Multi-site experience including carrier circuit management and redundant path failover Direct, hands-on firewall rule administration — creating, reviewing, and removing rules under a change process Enterprise wireless deployment and troubleshooting Strongly Preferred Experience Built centralized logging, monitoring, or SIEM capability from the ground up, including choosing what to collect, configuring retention, and tuning alerts. This is the highest-value qualification for this role. Network segmentation in a regulated or production environment — healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or PCI-scoped Wireless deployment supporting handheld scanners or mobile equipment in a warehouse, production floor, or clinical setting Participation in security incident response, including containment and post-incident documentation Producing evidence for compliance audits (HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST) Trainable — Not Required HIPAA and SOC 2 specifics, pharmacy operations, and USP 797/800 controlled-area procedures. Candidates with PCI, clinical, or manufacturing OT backgrounds carry transferable instincts and should not be screened out for lacking healthcare experience. This role is responsible for the design, deployment, operation, and troubleshooting of large-scale network environments that support critical business and engineering operations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who thrives in a fast-paced environment, possesses strong troubleshooting skills, and is comfortable working onsite to support infrastructure deployments, operational escalationns, project execution, and network incidents. Key Responsibilities Design, deploy, and support enterprise, campus, data center, and WAN network infrastructure. Configure and troubleshoot routing protocols including BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, and static routing. Support network technologies including routing, switching, wireless, network security, DNS, DHCP, and load balancing. Perform onsite troubleshooting of network, server, and application connectivity issues. Lead network upgrades, hardware refreshes, migrations, and infrastructure expansion projects. Develop and maintain network documentation, diagrams, standards, and operational procedures. Analyze packet captures, routing tables, logs, and monitoring data to identify and resolve complex network issues. Support data center networking technologies and high-availability network designs. Assist with cloud networking integration across Azure, AWS, and other cloud platforms. Participate in incident response, root cause analysis (RCA), and operational reviews. Collaborate with server, storage, cloud, security, and application teams to deliver infrastructure solutions. Utilize network monitoring and analytics platforms to proactively identify and resolve issues. Participate in on-call support and maintenance activities as required. Contribute to automation initiatives through scripting and operational efficiency improvements. Required Qualifications 7+ years of enterprise network engineering experience. Strong hands-on experience with enterprise routing and switching technologies. Experience supporting medium to large-scale enterprise and data center environments. Strong understanding of Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking concepts. Experience with routing protocols including BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP. Experience supporting Cisco, Arista, Aruba, or similar enterprise networking platforms. Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex production issues. Excellent communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work effectively in an onsite operational environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience with data center networking architectures and modern network design principles. Experience supporting cloud networking environments including Azure, AWS, or GCP. Familiarity with SD-WAN technologies and internet connectivity solutions. Experience with network automation using Python, Ansible, Terraform, or similar tools. Experience with monitoring and management platforms such as ThousandEyes, Splunk, SolarWinds, or similar technologies. Knowledge of DNS, DHCP, IPAM, and network security technologies. Industry certifications such as CCNP, CCIE, JNCIP, or equivalent.

review_candidates.title: Senior Lead Infrastructure Engineer — On Prem OpenShift Platform
review_candidates.description: Job Description We're looking for a talented, senior engineering professional ready to take their career to new heights at one of the world's most influential companies. As a Senior Lead Infrastructure Engineer at JPMorgan Chase within Enterprise Technology Compute Infrastructure Platforms team, you will design, engineer, and operate an on-premises OpenShift-based platform that hosts both containers and virtual machines (e.g., OpenShift Virtualization / KubeVirt). You will own the underlying infrastructure and OpenShift cluster foundations, compute, hypervisor platforms, operating systems, networking, storage, security controls, and reliability enabling product teams to deploy workloads safely, consistently, and efficiently. This is an infrastructure engineering role focused on platform lifecycle and reliability, partnering closely with hardware engineering, networking, storage, security, identity/access, and platform consumers. Job Responsibilities Design OpenShift cluster architectures (on-premises and/or hybrid) to meet availability, scalability, security, and operability requirements. Build and operate OpenShift clusters end-to-end, including install, upgrade, patching, scaling, resilience testing as well as virtualization capabilities supporting VM lifecycle (images/templates and relevant hardware acceleration concepts such as SR-IOV/DPDK/GPU passthrough, where applicable). Engineer the platform to support both Kubernetes workloads and VM workloads, including capacity planning, performance management, placement strategies, and HA/DR considerations. Own Linux platform fundamentals (e.g., RHEL/CoreOS concepts, kernel/sysctl tuning, certificates, and identity integration basics) required for reliable cluster operations. Implement and troubleshoot core networking capabilities (routing/switching fundamentals, DNS, L4/L7 concepts, load balancing, firewalling, segmentation, and packet-path analysis). Integrate storage services for container and VM workloads (block/file/object concepts, CSI drivers, performance and failure modes, and backup/restore approaches). Drive reliability practices including observability, incident response, root-cause analysis, and preventative improvements across the platform lifecycle. Develop runbooks, standards, and reference architectures; lead operational readiness reviews and post-incident actions. Uses enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate analysis of complex infrastructure signals and documentation of mitigation options, validating outputs and handling operational data according to sensitivity and security requirements. Leads reuse-first adoption of AI-assisted practices across delivery and automation routines to reduce recurring issues, ensuring changes are validated, traceable and auditable, and aligned to resiliency and security expectations. Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills Formal training or certification on infrastructure engineering concepts and 5+ years applied experience. Hands-on administration of Red Hat OpenShift and Kubernetes in production environments (e.g., install/upgrade patterns such as IPI/UPI, Operators, SCC/RBAC, cluster operators, ingress). Experience operating Kubernetes/container platforms through day-2 operations (upgrades, scaling, troubleshooting, and platform lifecycle management). Experience with OpenShift Virtualization / KubeVirt (or equivalent VM-on-Kubernetes) and VM/container co-tenancy design considerations. Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting experience (e.g., system performance, certificates, OS configuration, and cluster node operations). Demonstrated troubleshooting depth in at least two of the following domains: networking, storage, virtualization. Experience designing and operating highly available platforms, including capacity management, incident handling, root-cause analysis, and remediation tracking. Experience partnering with security/compliance stakeholders on hardening, RBAC, secrets/certificates handling, and vulnerability management aligned to secure-by-default configurations. Experience implementing infrastructure automation and configuration-as-code practices (e.g., Ansible/Terraform/GitOps patterns) with traceability and auditability. Demonstrated experience using enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to support infrastructure engineering workflows with strong validation habits and awareness of data sensitivity. Ability to review and validate AI-assisted recommendations before implementation, escalating when uncertain and ensuring outcomes align to resiliency, security, and auditability expectations. Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills Familiarity with OpenShift observability stacks (Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager, logging, tracing) and operational maturity practices. Experience with service mesh, ingress controllers, API gateways, or platform networking plugins aligned to your stack. Experience with enterprise storage technologies and their performance/failure characteristics in containerized environments. Familiarity using generative AI tools to accelerate research, troubleshooting, and documentation workflows (with appropriate governance). ABOUT US JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management. We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process. We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation. JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans About The Team Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

review_candidates.title: NetOps System Administrator
review_candidates.description: Company Overview By Light Professional IT Services LLC readies warfighters and federal agencies with technology and systems engineered to connect, protect, and prepare individuals and teams for whatever comes next. Headquartered in McLean, VA, By Light supports defense, civilian, and commercial IT customers worldwide. Cole Engineering Services (CESI), a By Light company, is recognized as a premier provider of modeling and simulation (M&S) training solutions to the Federal Government and industry. Since 2004, CESI has been at the forefront of developing, maintaining, and integrating simulation-based training, serious gaming, technical services, training and other support in live, virtual, constructive, and gaming (LVCG) domains. CESI also designs, builds and runs infrastructure, platforms, applications and processes that enable cyber training for the integrated multi-domain force. Our vision is to become a worldwide full spectrum LVCG and cyber training/analysis developer, integrator and services provider. Position Overview The Network Operations (NetOps) System Administrator is a critical member of the team responsible for providing top-tier IT support in a multifaceted and dynamic environment. This position conducts the daily operations, performance, and availability of network infrastructure and services. The role serves as a primary point of coordination for network operations activities, ensuring the high availability, security, and performance of mission-critical systems across multiple environments. Specifically, the NetOps System Administrator monitors network performance, executes incident response and reporting, collects and analyzes platform metrics, and contributes to the development of operational policies and procedures. This is a full time position on-site in Annapolis Junction, MD. PCTE support operates 24x7x365, this shift is Saturday and Sunday, 2000-0800; and two weekdays 0800-1600. Responsibilities Ensure efficient and secure operations across all supported systems and networks. Perform day-to-day network performance monitoring. Collect & analyze metrics and trending data, develop data standards, policies, and procedures. Analyzes data sources, assesses validity, and provides actionable recommendations. Conduct incident response activities, ensuring timely triage, escalation, resolution, and documentation of network-related issues. Prepare and present operational briefings, status reports, and performance metrics to leadership, ensuring informed decision-making. Develop and manage detailed documentation to support standardized operational processes and procedures. Maintain awareness of system capacity, utilization trends, and potential performance bottlenecks. Required Experience/Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline such as IT, computer science, systems or software engineering from an accredited college or university. (5 years’ experience in lieu of degree). DoD 8140/8570 IAT Level II or greater certification such as Security+, CCNA, CISSP or other equivalent certification within six months of hire. 4+ years of directly related experience supporting help desk operations. Two to five years of analytics tools such as Metabase and Grafana. Experience with VMware, Net App, and RedHat Linux (RHEL). Self-starter in a fast-paced environment, collaborating with engineers of varying skills and experience levels. Effective written and oral communication with leadership on both business and technical aspects. Experience supporting virtualized and cloud-hosted environments. Experience using ticketing and incident management platforms such as ServiceNow or Jira. Preferred Experience/Qualifications Knowledge of, or prior experience with PCTE. Problem-solving skills for resolving technical issues across diverse integrated software and hardware platforms. Experience with database and model design and segmentation techniques. Proficiency in generating queries and reports, utilizing data analysis tools such as Excel, Meta Base, and SPSS. Strong ability to prioritize multiple tasks, projects, and demands. Effective communication with vendors, users, customers, and developers to comprehend needs and operational requirements changes impacting the production environment. Proven success in a collaborative, team-oriented environment Special Requirements/Security Clearance Please note that pursuant to a government contract, this specific position requires U. S. Citizenship status and a TS/SCI security clearance. Security Clearance requirements will be specified in the Government's Task Order. Occasional travel may be required (as part of a mobile training team) up to 25% of the time. Salary Range Based on the roles, responsibilities, and requirements, the projected pay range for this position is: $110,000 - $130,000. The annual base salary provided is a guideline for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation or salary. When extending an offer, CESI also considers other variables such as (but not limited to) work experience, education, training, skill set, internal peer equity, clearance level, and market conditions. In addition, CESI provides an extensive selection of benefits and offerings to our employees. Benefits Overview CESI recognizes that our strength is our people. We support every employee as an individual to build strong teams across the enterprise. Our benefit package includes: Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage Wellness Program 401(k) Matching Disability (Short Term & Long Term) Employee Assistance Program Life Insurance Education & Training Generous Leave Policy (11 Federal Holidays, PTO, Military Leave, Bereavement and Jury Duty) CESI is committed to principles of inclusion and equal employment opportunity. We foster a non-discriminatory, professional work environment for all our teams. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

review_candidates.title: Platform Engineer — AWS Cloud
review_candidates.description: Axiom Space is a human space exploration company, building era-defining space infrastructure and delivering technology-driven solutions that will empower civilization to transcend Earth. Beginning with Axiom Station, successor to the International Space Station, the company is pioneering a next-generation orbital settlement that will foster groundbreaking innovation and research in microgravity and drive the global space economy of tomorrow. Today, guided by the vision of leading humanity's expansion off planet, Axiom Space is the principal provider of commercial human spaceflight services and developer of advanced spacesuits for the Moon and beyond. For more information about Axiom Space, visit www.axiomspace.com. Axiom Space fosters a work environment inclusive of all perspectives. We are the pioneers of commercial space, leading the transformation of low-Earth orbit into a global space marketplace. Our mission-driven team is seeking a bold and dynamic Platform Engineer (AWS Cloud) who is fueled by high accountability, execution horsepower, and driven to understand our world, science/technology, and life itself, for the benefit of all on Earth and beyond. Position Summary Since Axiom Space is a very complex work environment, we are looking for a resilient, high-energy Platform Engineer (AWS Cloud), who designs, builds, and operates the AWS-first cloud infrastructure that Axiom's engineering and business teams run on. This person drives automation, infrastructure-as-code, and platform reliability practices that let internal teams ship faster and safer, while maintaining working familiarity with Azure and Microsoft 365 to support occasional cross-platform workloads. This role serves as an escalation point for platform architecture and technical issues beyond the scope of entry-level engineers, and contributes to the continuous improvement of Axiom's enterprise cyber security program under the direction of senior IT leadership. Key Duties & Responsibilities Designs, builds, and maintains infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or CloudFormation) to provision and manage AWS GovCloud environments — accounts, networking (VPC), and compute — in a repeatable, version-controlled way via AWS Landing Zone Accelerator (LZA) based architecture Serves as the primary escalation point for AWS platform architecture, systems design, and technical issues beyond the scope of entry-level engineers Builds and maintains CI/CD pipelines (AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins) that automate build, test, and deployment workflows for internal engineering teams Administers and evolves Axiom's AWS environment as the primary cloud platform — accounts, networking, compute, and core services (EC2, S3, and related) Builds and maintains container and orchestration platforms (Docker, Kubernetes/EKS) to support internal application workloads Manages identity and access management (IAM) within AWS IAM and supports SSO/SAML/SCIM integrations, ensuring least-privilege access across the platform Implements monitoring, logging, and observability (e.g., CloudWatch) to track platform health, and reviews incidents and performance data to determine root cause and drive remediation Preserves platform assets by implementing disaster recovery and backup automation, and develops, maintains, and tests business continuity plans for cloud environments Develops and maintains internal tooling and self-service capabilities that give engineering teams safe, automated access to the AWS platform Recommends cloud platform engineering strategies, tooling, and standards by evaluating organizational outcomes, identifying problems, and anticipating requirements May provide technical guidance to entry-level platform and IT engineers and review their AWS-related work as needed Maintains basic working familiarity with Azure and Microsoft 365 administration to support occasional cross-platform workloads Communicating project progress, status, and potential issues to stakeholders and leadership Implementing and maintaining agile project management methodologies throughout the project lifecycle Perform additional job duties as assigned Qualifications To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Education & Experience The majority of that experience should be spent building and operating production workloads on AWS Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Engineering Science, or Engineering Management, 4+ years of experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience Track record of making things happen in ambiguous, fast-moving environments Uses good judgement to problem-solve proactively, positively impacting hard challenges Demonstrated organization skills to meet tight deadlines with high quality results Core Skills Passion for space and the mission Entrepreneurial, growth mindset High EQ and ability to collaborate within teams and cross-functionally Tech-solutioning in using systems and tools to move smarter and faster Computer Skills To perform this job successfully, an individual should have knowledge of: Strong AWS administration (IAM, VPC networking, EC2/compute, S3, and core services) as the primary cloud platform — deep, hands-on expertise expected Infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform or CloudFormation) and configuration management (Ansible or equivalent) CI/CD pipeline experience (AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins) and scripting proficiency in Python or Bash Containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes/EKS, or equivalent) Identity and access management (IAM): users, groups, roles, and least-privilege policy design within AWS Working knowledge of Azure Cloud administration (compute, networking, storage, governance) and Microsoft 365 (including SharePoint and OneDrive administration) sufficient to support occasional Azure-hosted workloads General server hardware familiarity (Windows and Linux), general IT security and firewall management, and backup administration experience Wired and wireless networking, DHCP, and DNS; virtualization via VMware or equivalent; patch management via Windows Update or third-party Storage administration (users, access controls, and content governance across cloud storage) Preferred Certifications Candidates holding one or more of the following are strongly preferred: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate or Professional AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate Core Competencies Embody our core values of leadership , innovation , and teamwork. This position requires deep technical expertise in firewall and network security engineering, strong leadership capabilities, and the ability to collaborate effectively with NASA senior leadership, program management, cybersecurity leads, and cross-functional engineering teams. Key Responsibilities Lead the Firewall Engineering Architecture Team, providing technical direction for enterprise firewall, IDS/IPS, and security control design and integration. Define NASA’s enterprise firewall architecture strategy, ensuring alignment with zero-trust, mission-security, and risk management requirements. Serve as the senior technical authority and escalation point for complex firewall, perimeter security, and cross-domain protection issues. Develop modernization roadmaps and standards for firewall performance, resiliency, rule/policy lifecycle management, and automation. Oversee large-scale firewall migrations, data center and cloud integrations, and enterprise segmentation initiatives. Partner with NASA and Leidos leadership to support proposals, technical volumes, and Basis of Estimates (BOEs) related to security architecture efforts. Drive innovation in areas such as firewall automation, orchestration, SDN-based security, cloud-native firewalls, and threat visibility enhancements. Establish governance processes for rule validation, configuration baselines, policy stewardship, and continuous monitoring. Mentor engineers, establish training pipelines, and promote technical rigor and standardization across the Firewall Engineering discipline. Deliver data-driven technical briefings and executive-level recommendations to NASA and Leidos senior management. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field (Master’s preferred). 8–12 years of experience in enterprise network security or firewall engineering, with 8–10 years serving in senior engineering, architectural, or leadership roles. Deep expertise with next-generation firewall platforms (e.g., Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco, Juniper) and enterprise-grade security services. Strong understanding of network architecture, routing/switching, zero-trust principles, intrusion detection/prevention, and segmentation strategies. Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering teams in complex, high-visibility operational environments. Host online troubleshooting and investigation sessions on customer production environments running on legacy Windows and Linux servers as well as Kubernetes-orchestrated infrastructure. Collect and document all necessary problem details, logs, and diagnostic data pulled from legacy Windows/Linux hosts and Kubernetes cluster telemetry alike to drive effective, evidence-based resolution. The ideal candidate will possess a strong background in capital markets, hands-on expertise in Linux/Unix environments, deep knowledge of the FIX protocol, and a proven track record of supporting high-touch trading desks, Direct Market Access (DMA), and algorithmic trading platforms. You will bridge the gap between infrastructure operations, development teams, and business stakeholders to maintain a seamless trading environment. Batch Scheduling & Automation: Design, configure, monitor, and troubleshoot batch jobs using Autosys to automate critical operational workflows and data processing. System Operations: Perform daily Start of Day (SOD) and End of Day (EOD) activities on Linux systems to guarantee environment availability for live trading. Database Support: Query and manage relational databases (SQL, Postgres, Oracle) to fetch data, analyze table partitions, and support data warehousing requirements. Application & Connectivity Support FIX Connectivity Management: Lead the functional enhancement, configuration, and monitoring of the FIX connectivity platform. Manage client onboarding, UAT testing, and certification of FIX algos. Trading Desk Support: Provide on-floor L1/L2 production support to high-touch trading desks for equities, futures, and options, as well as DMA and algorithmic trading desks. Exchange Connectivity: Coordinate and execute exchange connectivity tasks, including uploading exchange files, margin/position files, and participating in regular exchange mock trading sessions (e.g., NSE/BSE). Vendor & Developer Collaboration: Act as the primary technical liaison with third-party application vendors (e.g., Omnesys, Traderpath) and internal development teams to resolve complex application bugs and deploy backend fixes. Monitoring, Incident & Change Management Proactive Monitoring: Utilize enterprise monitoring tools such as ITRS Geneos to track system health, latency, and connectivity, proactively addressing alerts before they impact the business. Incident Resolution: Own and manage production incidents from detection through to resolution. Perform root cause analysis (RCA) and raise/track tickets in ServiceNow and Jira. Change & Release Management: Schedule, coordinate, and deploy production changes, software packages, and drivers on servers during non-market hours, adhering to strict change control policies. Regulatory Reporting: Ensure timely processing and transfer of operational and transaction files (e.g., OTR files) to regulatory bodies (e.g., SEBI) and clients. Required Technical Skills & Qualifications Experience & Education Experience: Minimum of 7+ years of experience in production support, application support, or infrastructure operations within the Capital Markets / Investment Banking domain. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electronics & Telecommunications, Computer Science, or a related technical field). Technical Competencies Operating Systems: Strong administration and troubleshooting skills in Linux/Unix and Windows environments. Scripting: Proficiency in Unix Shell Scripting for task automation, log analysis, and data extraction. Protocols: Deep understanding of FIX Protocols (session and application levels) and FIX configuration. Databases: Solid experience writing SQL queries and working with Postgres, Oracle, or SQL Server. Tools & Applications: Scheduling: Autosys Monitoring: ITRS Geneos Ticketing/Collaboration: ServiceNow, Jira Trading Applications: Experience with trading platforms (e.g., Omnesys, Traderpath, Gatelab HFT, Bloomberg) is highly desirable. Soft Skills & Domain Knowledge Domain Expertise: Comprehensive understanding of capital markets, equity/derivatives trading lifecycles, and high-frequency trading (HFT) concepts. Stakeholder Management: Ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders, including Institutional Sales, Execution Traders, QA, Compliance, and external vendors. Collect the environment details required to reproduce and diagnose an issue (OS and version, agent version, hosting control panel, relevant logs, affected paths) before escalating, so engineering starts with a full picture instead of a thread of follow-up questions. Escalate well. Route complex or security-sensitive incidents to engineering and product with a clear written summary of what was observed, what was tried, and what's needed. Pulling in senior staff when the situation calls for it. Own our AI support tooling. Take ownership of the AI agent in Intercom. Curate the content and knowledge sources it draws on, review its conversations for wrong or incomplete answers, tune when it should resolve versus hand off to a human, and steadily expand the range of questions it can handle on its own. Own the knowledge base. Maintain and improve support documentation, help center articles, and internal runbooks. Written both for customers and to be machine-readable enough that the AI answers from them accurately. Close the feedback loop. Track ticket trends and AI deflection and escalation rates, identify recurring root causes and content gaps, and flag them to the product team as candidates for a real fix. Who we're looking for Required Direct experience at or with a web hosting provider. Deployment, provisioning, fleet management, or support Exposure to configuration management and automation tooling (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt) or container and virtualization platforms (Docker, LXC, KVM) Comfort with Linux command-line troubleshooting. Navigating a filesystem, package managers (yum/dnf, apt), services, and reading logs to find the relevant signal Clear, precise written communication, especially the ability to explain a technical issue to a customer without oversimplifying or overwhelming them Sound judgment about prioritization, and a good instinct for when to resolve independently versus when to escalate Comfort working directly with customers on issues that are urgent, ambiguous, or both Experience writing and maintaining support documentation or a customer-facing knowledge base Interest in using AI support tooling as a real part of the job, and the judgment to tell a good automated answer from a confidently wrong one Genuine interest in how hosting companies operate, deploy, and manage servers at scale. We'll teach you what you don't already know, but the curiosity has to be there Nice to have Hands-on experience with Intercom, particularly its AI agent / Fin, or a comparable AI-driven support platform Working understanding of security concepts: malware behavior, detection logic, false positives and false negatives Scripting ability (bash, Python) for pulling diagnostics together Experience with a ticketing or support platform and with SLA-driven workflows Support coverage and on-call Our customers run production infrastructure across multiple time zones, so support availability matters. We're location agnostic for this role, with a slight preference for Europe. Core coverage: Monday–Friday business hours in your local time zone Participation in a shared after-hours rotation for security-sensitive and production-impacting incidents Escalation path to senior engineering is available at all times; you are never expected to solve a critical incident alone What We Offer Competitive salary with equity opportunities. Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision. Flexible PTO policy. Remote working environment

Participate in incident response and troubleshooting for CI/CD and developer tooling issues following established operational procedures. Create and maintain technical documentation related to pipeline configurations, GitOps patterns, Artifactory setup, and troubleshooting steps. Collaborate with senior engineers, application teams, and partner engineering groups to understand requirements and implement developer toolchain Participate in on-call rotations and scheduled maintenance windows with guidance from senior team members. Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containerized platforms; experience with Red Hat OpenShift is strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience administering or supporting MongoDB or PostgreSQL platforms deployed on Kubernetes-based environments. Working knowledge of Linux operating systems and system administration Familiarity with CI/CD tooling such as GitHub, Jenkins, Codefresh, and Git- based workflows. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot distributed systems issues with guidance. Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate within a team environment. We operate with the speed and agility of a startup within the world's largest professional services firm. We drive value for our clients by optimizing decisions and actions at a level of granularity only made possible with today's data and technology. ConvergeCONSUMER's suite of solutions helps consumer-facing businesses prosper in a world being re-shaped by convergence, where the lines between industries, competitors and collaborators, consumers and suppliers, and even human and artificial intelligence have blurred. Our approach for addressing this complexity is simple: we combine Deloitte's next-generation technology platforms with decades of experience in the consumer sector and a deep understanding of its unique issues and challenges to drive profitability and future growth for our clients. Position Summary Cloud Engineering & Deployment, Expert Services Are you a hands-on cloud engineer who thrives on turning complex deployments into smooth, repeatable rollouts? As a Product Installation Engineer with ConvergeCONSUMER, you'll bring our suite of AI-driven products to life inside the cloud environments of some of the world's most influential consumer businesses. If you enjoy solving real infrastructure problems under real client conditions, we'd like to talk with you. Recruiting for this role ends on 9/30/2026. Work you'll do As the Product Installation Engineer within Expert Services, you will be responsible for installing one of a suite of applications, all following the same pattern of containerized applications with a React front end and Python business logic, into clients' cloud environments or on-premises data centers. This role requires hands-on expertise in instantiating and managing containerized applications, with a strong focus on cloud engineering, infrastructure provisioning, observability, and traceability. Key Responsibilities: Install and deploy containerized applications into clients' cloud environments or data centers. Manage and maintain containerized applications to ensure optimal performance and reliability. Collaborate with cloud engineering and security organizations to ensure infrastructure is provisioned correctly. Test the basic functionality of cloud applications to declare them open for business. Adapt logging and monitoring hooks to integrate with clients' native operations, ensuring observability and traceability. Assist the developer team with remote debugging and troubleshooting issues. Automate deployment processes to achieve quick time to value for clients. Communicate technical requirements for cloud deployments clearly, including concepts like access groups, roles, permissions, and networking. Work with common cloud infrastructure components such as VPCs, managed services, and storage solutions. Manage data ingress and egress requirements, including moving large datasets within cloud contexts and across cloud instances. Ensure compliance with clients' security and operational standards. Stay up-to-date with the latest industry trends, tools, and technologies to continuously improve deployment practices and processes. The successful candidate would possess these skills: Hands-on approach to deploying and managing containerized applications in complex, client-facing cloud environments, with a strong bias toward reliability, repeatability, and quick time to value. Deep familiarity with cloud infrastructure fundamentals, including VPCs, managed services, storage solutions, access groups, roles, and permissions, and the ability to communicate these concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical client stakeholders. Strong infrastructure-as-code instincts, with the ability to automate and standardize deployment processes across varied client environments and data centers. Comfort operating at the intersection of cloud engineering and security, collaborating with client infrastructure and security organizations to ensure compliant, correctly provisioned deployments. Proven ability to adapt observability and monitoring frameworks to client-native operations, ensuring traceability and operational continuity post-deployment. Methodical troubleshooting approach with experience supporting remote debugging and resolving complex deployment issues in collaboration with developer teams. Fluency in data ingress and egress requirements, including the ability to move and manage large datasets within and across cloud environments. Curiosity for emerging cloud technologies and deployment practices, with a continuous improvement mindset that keeps pace with a rapidly evolving infrastructure landscape. Qualifications Required: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. 5+ years of professional cloud engineering experience. Ability to travel 25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future. The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $116,200-$229,100. You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

review_candidates.title: Principal Database Engineer – SQL Server & AI Data Infrastructure
review_candidates.description: Principal Database Engineer – SQL Server & AI Data Infrastructure The Opportunity WEX is looking for a highly experienced Database Engineer to help modernize and scale critical data platforms while supporting the next generation of AI-enabled applications. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who brings deep expertise in SQL Server and T-SQL, combined with the ability to solve complex database performance, scalability, and modernization challenges at enterprise scale. You will work across large, business-critical data environments, partnering closely with application engineering, SRE, operations, and architecture teams. The role is highly technical and execution-oriented—you will be expected to independently identify problems, drive solutions, and take ownership from design through implementation and production. The team is also applying modern AI capabilities to database engineering, including AI-assisted development, automation, semantic search, embeddings, and vector-based data infrastructure. What You'll Do Database Engineering & Modernization Design, develop, optimize, and modernize large-scale SQL Server databases and data platforms. Analyze and refactor complex T-SQL, stored procedures, functions, and database logic. Identify and resolve database performance bottlenecks through execution-plan analysis, indexing, query optimization, and database tuning. Drive schema improvements and database modernization initiatives that improve scalability, maintainability, and reliability. Develop migration strategies and automation that maintain data integrity and minimize disruption to business-critical systems. Implement and improve data replication and synchronization patterns across transactional and analytical environments. Apply event-driven database patterns such as Change Data Capture (CDC), outbox patterns, and event publishing. Enterprise-Scale Data Platforms Engineer solutions for large, high-volume databases supporting critical business applications and partners. Work with databases containing terabytes of data and complex data relationships. Develop data pipelines and integration patterns across SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and cloud data services. Support both OLTP and OLAP environments and optimize data movement between systems. Apply strong understanding of database internals, including indexing, locking, transactions, isolation levels, concurrency, and query optimization. AI-Enabled Database Engineering Use modern AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar tools to accelerate development, analysis, debugging, and modernization. Explore and implement AI-powered approaches for analyzing stored procedures, documenting schemas, and automating database engineering workflows. Contribute to AI-native data infrastructure, including embedding pipelines, vector databases, semantic search, and retrieval systems. Develop data and retrieval capabilities that support AI applications and agentic workflows. Evaluate emerging AI tools and determine where they can improve engineering productivity and data platform capabilities. Technical Leadership & Ownership Independently lead complex database engineering initiatives from problem definition through production implementation. Serve as a technical resource for complex database and performance challenges. Partner effectively with application engineering, SRE, operations, architecture, and AI/ML teams. Provide technical guidance through code reviews, design discussions, and engineering standards. Mentor other engineers and contribute to the development of database engineering practices. Take ownership of outcomes rather than simply completing assigned tasks. Production & Problem Solving Participate in resolving high-impact production issues involving critical database systems. Diagnose complex problems using logs, database metrics, CPU/memory utilization, execution plans, and other observability data. Quickly determine root cause, coordinate with the appropriate technical teams, and drive issues through resolution. Balance immediate incident resolution with longer-term improvements that prevent recurrence. What You'll Bring Required Experience 15+ years of experience in database engineering, data platform engineering, software engineering, or a related technical discipline. Deep hands-on experience with Microsoft SQL Server and T-SQL, including complex stored procedures, query optimization, execution-plan analysis, indexing, and performance tuning. Demonstrated experience modernizing or refactoring legacy database systems, not simply maintaining existing environments. Experience working with large-scale, business-critical databases and high-volume data environments. Strong programming skills in Python, C#, or a similar language for automation, tooling, and data processing. Experience with data pipelines, ETL/ELT, data integration, batch processing, and/or event-driven architectures. Strong understanding of database internals, transaction management, concurrency, locking, and performance optimization. Experience working across engineering teams and independently driving complex technical initiatives. AI & Modern Data Technologies Experience using AI coding assistants such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Augment, or similar tools. Familiarity with embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, or RAG concepts. Experience with or willingness to build AI-enabled data tooling and automation. Exposure to technologies such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, AWS data services, or similar platforms. Cloud & Engineering Practices Experience with infrastructure-as-code such as Terraform, ARM/Bicep, or similar technologies. Experience with CI/CD, source control, database migrations, schema versioning, and deployment automation. Experience with event streaming technologies such as Kafka is a plus. Familiarity with NoSQL and document databases is a plus. Preferred Experience Experience in payments, financial services, healthcare, benefits, or other highly regulated environments. Experience supporting highly available, customer-facing or business-critical systems. Experience with Oracle PL/SQL in addition to SQL Server. Hands-on experience with RAG, semantic search, vector databases, or AI-agent data infrastructure. Experience building internal engineering tools or automation using AI. Why This Role Matters WEX operates at a significant enterprise scale, and our database platforms are foundational to critical customer and business experiences. This role sits at the intersection of deep database engineering, large-scale modernization, cloud data platforms, and emerging AI technologies. You will have the opportunity to apply proven database engineering expertise to some of the industry's most challenging data problems while helping shape how AI can transform the way modern engineering teams build, operate, and evolve data platforms. This is an opportunity for an engineer who wants to remain deeply technical while operating with the ownership and influence expected at the Senior Staff level. The base pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the pay range for this position. Actual pay rates will vary and will be based on various factors, such as your qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Base pay is one component of WEX's total compensation package. Most sales positions are eligible for commission under the terms of an applicable plan. Non-sales roles are typically eligible for a quarterly or annual bonus based on their role and applicable plan. WEX's comprehensive and market competitive benefits are designed to support your personal and professional well-being. Benefits include health, dental and vision insurances, retirement savings plan, paid time off, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability insurance, tuition reimbursement, and more. For more information, check out the "About Us" section. Pay Range: $165,800.00 - $204,400.00

review_candidates.description: Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences. Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team. Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team.
