About The Role As a Backend Software Engineer on the Data Layer team, you'll help build and evolve the storage and query layer that keeps Camunda 8's process data fast, accurate, and available at scale. Spanning both relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, the data layer and its data pipelines power everything from process monitoring to the new agent-driven automation capabilities we're rolling out. As part of the Data Layer team, you will work on both technically challenging and rewarding projects, such as reshaping how we store and retain process data, streaming data to external systems, and evolving our secondary storage systems to perform at ever greater scale. At Camunda, we approach engineering in a holistic manner. As such, you will form strong partnerships with product management, design, QA, and support, and work with your peers to not only deliver but directly influence how our data layer evolves to meet our customers' needs. Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale What You’ll Be Doing Design, build, and maintain backend services for the data layer that stores and serves Camunda 8's process data, spanning relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, with an eye toward correctness, performance, and scale. Own the end-to-end delivery of engineering initiatives, working with Product Management and senior colleagues to break down requirements into concrete solution designs, driving projects to timely and high-quality delivery. Help evolve how we process, retain, and expose process data, so customers can work with their data the way they need to. Invest in making our secondary storage systems more performant and scalable as usage grows, and build tooling that makes it easier to understand, troubleshoot, and safely operate the data layer in production. Participate in L3 support and on-call rotations, partnering with Support and SRE to investigate data layer production issues, and feeding what you learn back into the product. What You Bring Ability and/or willingness to use our product At least 4 years of experience as a backend engineer, with a strong focus on backend systems and production data stores Hands-on experience with at least one of PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MSSQL, or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, with a practical understanding of query performance, indexing, and data modeling trade-offs Experience contributing to complex engineering initiatives: breaking down requirements into concrete tasks, writing clear technical designs for your piece of the work, and delivering reliably Comfortable investigating slow queries, execution plans, and index usage to root-cause data-related production issues. Strong communication and collaboration skills in a remote-first environment: you translate requirements into actionable technical work with Product, and give and receive clear, direct feedback in code review. Nice-to-haves Experience building workflow automation or process orchestration software. Experience working with both relational databases and Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Experience building or maintaining CI pipelines. Understanding of database migration tooling (e.g. Liquibase, Flyway) and schema evolution in a live system. new_matches.title: Tier 2 Infrastructure & Network Engineer - Prince George, BC
new_matches.description: About CORE Core Network Solutions Inc. is a Canadian managed IT services and network infrastructure company with more than 23 years of operation, serving over 150 clients across Western Canada from our head office in St. Albert, Alberta and our regional office in Prince George, British Columbia. We design, deploy and manage network, security and infrastructure environments for municipalities, health authorities and private-sector organizations — clients who expect their infrastructure to simply work, and who count on us when it doesn’t. Position Summary We are looking for a Tier 2 Infrastructure & Network Engineer to take a lead role in the design, deployment and ongoing operation of client network, virtualization and security environments. This is a hands-on senior role: you will own project delivery from design through cutover, act as the top escalation point for complex technical issues, and travel to client sites across Western Canada to deliver network implementations. The successful candidate is a broad, senior generalist — strong in enterprise networking, comfortable at a Linux command line, fluent in containerized and virtualized workloads, and confident configuring next-generation firewalls and web application firewalls. Key Responsibilities Network Implementation & Engineering •     Design, configure and deploy enterprise LAN, WAN, SD-WAN and wireless environments for client sites, including switching, routing, VLAN architecture and QoS. •     Lead network implementation projects end to end: requirements gathering, design documentation, bill of materials, staging and configuration, on-site installation, cutover and post-deployment validation. •     Configure and maintain routing and switching platforms across CORE’s core vendor lines, including Fortinet, Juniper, HPE, Arista and Check Point. •     Plan and execute network migrations and refreshes with minimal client disruption, including after-hours cutover windows. •     Implement and troubleshoot site-to-site and remote access VPN, including IPsec, IKEv2 and SSL VPN. •     Produce and maintain accurate network documentation: topology diagrams, IP schemas, configuration standards and as-built records. Linux Administration •     Deploy, harden, patch and administer Linux servers (Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL-family) in client and internal environments. •     Manage core Linux services including DNS, DHCP, NTP, SSH, web and reverse-proxy services, certificate management and log forwarding. •     Write and maintain shell scripts and lightweight automation to standardize repetitive administrative tasks. •     Perform Linux-level performance analysis and root cause investigation using standard diagnostic tooling. •     Apply security hardening baselines, manage user and privilege models, and support client audit and compliance requirements. Container & Docker Administration •     Deploy, configure and maintain Docker hosts and containerized workloads supporting client and internal services. •     Build and maintain container images, Docker Compose stacks, persistent storage and container networking. •     Monitor container health, resource consumption and logging; manage lifecycle, updates and image hygiene. •     Apply container security practices including image provenance, least-privilege runtime configuration and registry management. Cybersecurity — NGFW and WAF •     Deploy, configure and manage next-generation firewalls, including policy design, application control, IPS/IDS, URL filtering, TLS inspection and threat prevention profiles. •     Deploy and tune web application firewalls, including rule sets, policy exceptions, false-positive tuning and protection of published client applications. •     Implement network segmentation and zero-trust-aligned access policies across client environments. •     Support CORE’s CNSsecure security offerings and integrate deployed controls with client monitoring and reporting. •     Investigate security events, analyze firewall and system logs, and produce clear post-incident findings for clients. •     Stay current with emerging threats, vendor advisories and firmware and security patching cycles across managed platforms. Hypervisor Deployment & Management •     Design, deploy and manage virtualization platforms including Proxmox VE, Microsoft Hyper-V and Morpheus. •     Build and maintain clustered hypervisor environments including shared storage, high availability and live migration. •     Manage virtual machine lifecycle: provisioning, templating, resource allocation, snapshots and capacity planning. •     Configure virtual networking, distributed switching and hypervisor-level segmentation. •     Integrate virtualization platforms with backup and recovery tooling, and regularly validate restore capability. •     Perform hypervisor upgrades, patching and migrations between platforms. Project Travel & On-Site Delivery •     Travel to client sites across Alberta, British Columbia and Western Canada to deliver network and infrastructure implementations — approximately 25% of working time, typically in multi-day blocks scheduled in advance. •     Perform physical installation work: rack and stack, structured cabling termination and dressing, device mounting, labelling and equipment decommissioning. Troubleshooting & Analysis •     Serve as the senior escalation point for complex, cross-domain issues spanning network, server, virtualization and security layers. •     Apply a structured diagnostic method — reproduce, isolate the fault domain, test hypotheses, confirm root cause, remediate — rather than trial-and-error changes. •     Use packet capture and protocol analysis, log correlation and performance monitoring tooling to resolve issues others could not. •     Document root cause analyses and feed findings back into standards, monitoring and preventative maintenance. •     Mentor intermediate and junior technical staff in diagnostic technique and escalation discipline. Client Service & Managed Services Delivery •     Meet service level commitments and communicate proactively when timelines or scope change. •     Communicate directly with client technical and non-technical stakeholders •     Maintain client documentation to CORE standards •     Contribute to scoping, estimating and technical review of proposals and statements of work. •     Participate in the on-call rotation and after-hours maintenance windows as scheduled. Qualifications Required •     6–10+ years of progressive experience in network and infrastructure engineering, ideally including time with a managed services provider, VAR or multi-client consulting firm. •     Demonstrated experience leading network implementation projects end to end, on client sites. •     Strong hands-on enterprise routing and switching expertise, including VLANs, spanning tree, dynamic routing protocols and WAN/SD-WAN technologies. •     Solid Linux administration skills at the command line, including services, scripting, hardening and diagnostics. •     Practical Docker and container administration experience in a production context. •     Hands-on next-generation firewall experience — policy design, threat prevention, VPN and troubleshooting — plus working knowledge of web application firewalls. •     Hypervisor deployment and management experience with at least two of Proxmox VE, Hyper-V or Morpheus, and the capacity to become proficient in all three. •     Excellent troubleshooting and analytical ability across multiple technology layers. •     Strong written and verbal communication in English, including client-facing documentation. •     Valid Class 5 driver’s licence and a reliable vehicle for local and regional travel. •     Ability to pass criminal record and security clearance checks required by public-sector and health-sector clients. •     Legally entitled to work in Canada. Preferred •     Experience serving Canadian public-sector or health-sector clients (municipal, county, health authority). •     Familiarity with CORE’s primary vendor lines: Check Point, Fortinet, Juniper, HPE, Arista, Lenovo and Microsoft. •     Backup and disaster recovery experience, particularly where Canadian data residency is required. •     Infrastructure-as-code, configuration management or CI/CD exposure (Ansible, Terraform, Git-based workflows). •     Monitoring and observability tooling experience. •     Microsoft 365 and Entra ID / Active Directory administration. •     Experience mentoring or leading a small technical team. Certifications Certifications are valued, but demonstrated capability matters more. Any of the following are considered assets, and CORE supports certification pursuit for the right candidate. •     Security: Check Point CCSA / CCSE, Fortinet NSE 4–7, CompTIA Security+, SSCP •     Networking: Juniper JNCIA / JNCIS, JNCIP, JNCIE,Cisco CCNA / CCNP, CCIE, HPE Aruba ACSA / ACSP •     Linux: LPIC-1 / LPIC-2, Red Hat RHCSA / RHCE, CompTIA Linux+ •     Virtualization: Proxmox VE certification, Microsoft AZ-800 / AZ-801, VMware VCP •     Containers: Docker Certified Associate, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) Working Conditions •     Based at CORE’s Prince George, BC office, with a mix of office, client-site and remote work. •     Approximately 25% travel, primarily within Alberta and British Columbia, including occasional overnight and multi-day trips to rural and remote client sites. Travel is scheduled in advance wherever possible. •     Scheduled after-hours and weekend maintenance windows are a normal part of infrastructure cutover work. •     Participation in an on-call rotation. •     Physical requirements include lifting and positioning equipment up to approximately 50 lbs, working in server rooms and equipment closets. Core Network Solutions Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to providing accommodation for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process — please let us know if you require accommodation.

new_matches.title: Systems Consultant
new_matches.description: About CCT Founded in 2012, CCT pioneered revenue audit automation for land-based casinos, eliminating manual reconciliation and improving financial visibility. Our flagship platform, Casino Insight, provides a detailed, audit-ready view of cash transactions across the casino floor — supporting compliance, operational efficiency, and fraud prevention. Today CCT serves over 300 casinos across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. The Role Systems Consultants build and maintain the infrastructure that Casino Insight runs on. When a casino buys CCT, a Systems Consultant stands up the environment: Windows and SQL Server, the application and message-queue tiers, remote access, and the linkedserver connections that pull data out of the property's slot, table, cage, and sportsbook systems. After go-live, the same Systems Consultant owns that environment's health and is the escalation point when something breaks. It is a genuine consulting role. Most client IT departments are small, and many have never integrated a system like ours. You are the expert in the room — advising on architecture, negotiating firewall and access changes, and enabling the client's team to support their side of the deployment after handoff. You do this work from our Tulsa office, not from the casino floor. Nearly every environment build, upgrade, and troubleshooting session happens remotely over screen shares with client IT, so travel is under 10% — occasional go-live support, a client visit, or an industry event. Sitting with the team matters early on: this is a role you learn by overhearing how the person next to you talks a client's network admin through a firewall change. Systems Consultants who are established in the role have the opportunity to move to a hybrid schedule. What You'll Actually Do Build client environments (largest share of the role) Stand up application and database servers for new Insight Cash and Insight Analytics implementations — Windows Server, IIS, MS SQL Server, TLS certificates, service accounts, scheduled jobs Deploy and configure CCT's Data Bridge tier for single-site and multi-property clients Configure linked servers and third-party data connections across MSSQL, Oracle, AS400/DB2, and PostgreSQL — slot systems, ticketing, kiosks and recyclers, table games, sportsbook Set up employee Active Directory sync, report distribution, backups Cove, and training-environment refreshes from production Own the network and access layer Work with client IT to troubleshoot network issues between servers and workstations Establish AWS site-to-site VPN tunnels against client firewalls FortiGate, Palo Alto, Cisco ASA, pfSense, and others). If you've done this before, great — if you haven't, we'll teach you. Solid TCP/IP fundamentals matter more here than prior AWS experience Configure and maintain SecureLink remote access, including gatekeeper setup and audit review Support on-prem to AWS replication for hybrid client architectures Run upgrades and keep environments healthy Execute CAS push upgrades and MQ upgrades across the client base Diagnose and resolve escalated production issues — service failures, blocked ports, failed jobs, disk and performance problems, broken integrations Monitor environment health and patch levels; act on alerts before clients notice Consult and document Lead client IT kickoff calls: walk their team through requirements, architecture, and their responsibilities Produce clear technical documentation — configuration guides, environment records in Passportal, and knowledge-base articles the rest of the team relies on Support internal CCT IT and end-user requests as part of a shared rotation Tools you'll use: MS SQL Server / SSMS, Windows Server, Hyper-V, IIS, Active Directory, AWS VPC, VPN, EC2, S3, IAM, CloudWatch), SecureLink, Passportal, N Central, SentinelOne, Cove, Freshdesk, Mavenlink, Notion, GitHub, Slack. What Success Looks Like First 30 days: Local and lab environments built; oriented on the CCT stack; handling internal IT and enablement tickets with review First 60 days: Completing a full server environment build in lab independently; running Data Bridge deployments and upgrades in client environments with light supervision First 90 days: Owning a client environment build end-to-end, leading a client IT kickoff call, and handling standard support tickets without review New Systems Consultants work through a structured 90-day plan with a defined milestone checklist, shadowing time with each member of the team, and a specialty track chosen with your manager (networking, database, integrations, or internal IT. How We Expect You To Think This is the part of the job we care most about, and it's the part that's hardest to teach. Our documentation is good, and you will use it. However, a runbook cannot tell you why step 6 exists, what it assumes about the client's network, or what to do when the environment in front of you doesn't match the one the runbook was written against. Working through the steps without understanding the mechanism behind them is how a build passes every checkbox and still fails at go-live. What that looks like day to day: Understand the why before the how. You should be able to explain what a linked server actually does, why a VPN tunnel needs matching phase-2 selectors, or why a service account failed after a password policy change — not just recall the fix that worked last time. Diagnose, don't guess. Read the error. Check the log. Form a hypothesis, test the one thing that would disprove it, and narrow from there. Restarting services and re-running the installer until something changes is not troubleshooting. Know when you're outside what you understand. Being unsure is fine and expected — this stack is deep. Pretending otherwise in front of a client's IT director is not. Ask, escalate, or go read, then come back with an answer you can defend. Improve the process you inherited. When you find a gap, an undocumented step, or a step that exists only because someone once did it that way, say so and fix it. We would rather hear "this instruction is wrong and here's why" than watch it get followed for another two years. Be genuinely curious. The people who do well here take apart systems they've never seen because they want to know how they work, not because a ticket forced them to. Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in a technical field (Computer Science, MIS, Computer Engineering, etc.), or equivalent practical experience Hands-on proficiency with MS SQL Server (backup/restore, scheduled jobs, linked servers, permissions), Windows Server, Active Directory, and IIS Working knowledge of TCP/IP networking — firewalls, NAT, VPN concepts, DNS, certificates, port troubleshooting Excellent written and verbal communication; able to explain a technical requirement to a client's IT director and to write documentation someone else can follow Demonstrated troubleshooting discipline — a structured method for isolating a problem, and the ability to walk us through the reasoning behind a hard issue you solved, not just the outcome (see "How We Expect You to Think") Comfortable owning multiple client projects at once and driving them to a deadline without being managed day to day Ability to pass stringent background investigations and obtain gaming licensure/registration where required by client jurisdictions Preferred 3+ years in systems administration, infrastructure engineering, implementation consulting, or a comparable technical role AWS experience, especially VPC networking and site-to-site VPN — a real advantage, but something we're prepared to train Virtualization (Hyper-V, VMware) and cloud or hybrid infrastructure Exposure to Oracle, DB2/AS400, or PostgreSQL Scripting for automation (PowerShell, T SQL) Gaming, hospitality, or another regulated industry Relevant certifications (AWS, Microsoft, CompTIA Network+/Security+) Working Conditions Our team works on-site in the Tulsa, OK office, collaborating daily with client IT over calls and shared remote sessions. Hybrid flexibility opens up once you're established in the role Travel under 10% Casinos operate 24/7, so cutovers, upgrades, and go-lives are occasionally scheduled outside standard hours or on weekends. This is planned in advance, not routine On-call duty rotates weekly among the SC team, covering escalated production issues Work Authorization This position is not eligible for employer-sponsored work authorization or visa sponsorship (including initial, transfer, or extension). new_matches.title: Senior Core Infrastructure Engineer
new_matches.description: Job Description Designs, implements, and optimizes components in distributed systems with an emphasis on scalability, resiliency, and operability. Delivers features and load/performance tests; leverages data plane platforms and distributed state tools for high-volume retrieval, storage, and processing; and reviews peers’ implementations for scalability compliance. Builds fault-tolerant paths (redundancy, replication, automatic failover), applies recovery‑oriented principles, and implements retries, circuit breakers, and timeouts. Proactively detects and mitigates issues via tests, alarms, dashboards, and telemetry; authors runbooks and participates in incident response and RCAs. Implements standard replication and synchronization, develops automation/IaC for troubleshooting and maintenance, and applies advanced security controls (encryption, access, remediation) while ensuring change, compliance, and documentation standards are met. Responsibilities Key Responsibilities System Design & Architecture - System Scalability: –Implements and contributes to the development for components of distributed systems that support horizontal and vertical scaling including leveraging distributed state management tools. –Optimizes code and/or systems for large-scale data processing in large-scale systems. –Implements scalability requirements for assigned components and reviews implementation of team members. –Leverages components of data plane platforms to handle large-scale data retrieval, storage, and processing. –Implements performance and load testing. System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Design: –Collaborates with team to build fault-tolerant components capable of withstanding in-service updates by implementing redundancy, replication, and automatic failover mechanisms. –Applies recovery oriented computing principles to design components that effectively handle service disruptions. –Implements retry mechanisms, circuit breakers, and timeouts to help handle network unreliability. System Design & Architecture - System Reliability Performance: –Implements tests and alarm configurations to proactively detect and address issues/failures. –Supports efforts to recover from failures by drafting and executing runbooks and operational procedures. –Builds and customizes dashboards, telemetry systems, and alerting mechanisms to monitor component health. System Design & Architecture - Correctness / Availability: –Designs and implements functional requirements and testing for assigned features within an existing system. –Implements tests scenarios (e.g., fault-injection, brown-out) to evaluate system correctness. –Implements standard data replication and synchronization techniques to maintain data integrity and availability. Operational Troubleshooting & Incident Management: –Diagnoses, debugs, and resolves issues in system components to support ongoing operation. –Implements basic strategies to prevent interruptions, ensuring no maintenance windows are required for customers and users when resolving issues. –Designs and implements automation scripts and tooling used to troubleshoot operational issues. –Participates in operational support rotations, assisting in incident responses and root cause investigations. Compliance & Security: –Applies advanced security measures to protect data and applications in multi-tenant environments, including encryption and access controls. –Implements remediation plans to continuously improve security. –Collaborates with the team to ensure cloud infrastructure complies with relevant industry standards and regulations and that documentation is up-to-date Automation & Change Management: –Maintains automation scripts and tools (e.g., Infrastructure as Code (IaC)) for managing cloud infrastructure. –Adheres to change management plans for patching, updating, and rolling back applications. Core Responsibilities Planning & Execution: –Track timelines with minimal supervision, ensuring work is completed in a timely manner and is in alignment with project requirements. –Prioritize and adjust work as resources or timelines change, with some guidance Collaboration & Partnership: –Collaborates across teams to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives. Builds and maintains a comprehensive understanding of business, stakeholder, and/or customer needs to build and support effective partnerships. Actively listens to diverse perspectives and asks questions to ensure understanding of others. Problem Solving: –Independently identifies and addresses standard and non-standard issues in accordance with standard practices, escalating more complex issues as appropriate. Analyzes data and/or information from multiple sources to troubleshoot standard and non-standard errors. Contributes to knowledge sharing and best practices Continuous Learning: –Embraces continuous learning by actively seeking to build knowledge and new skills and/or tools, and staying current with industry trends and best practices. Seeks out and leverages feedback and training to improve skills. Contributes to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing with team members.. Continuous Improvement: –Develops ideas and recommends updates to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows within a team. Seeks input from team members on alternative approaches and methods for improving work. new_matches.title: Senior Operations Engineer
new_matches.description: Overview This role provides senior-level technical engineering and troubleshooting support for enterprise clients running hybrid environments that span legacy Windows and Linux systems and Kubernetes-based infrastructure. Responsibilities center on root-cause analysis of complex, multi-tier defects - reproducing issues in controlled environments, engineering fixes, and validating them through automated test suites. The role also carries direct ownership of delivery infrastructure: building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Azure DevOps), managing containerized workloads on AWS EKS (Helm, autoscaling, rolling deployments), and administering legacy server infrastructure - patching, hardening, and tuning -while supporting migration to Kubernetes. Observability tools such as CloudWatch, Prometheus/Grafana, or Datadog are used to monitor system health and resolve anomalies proactively. This person partners with Product, Development, and Implementation teams during release cycles and collaborates with distributed Product Operations peers, providing technical mentorship on legacy administration, containerization, and automation practices. Responsibilities Provide senior technical and operational support to enterprise clients for product-related issues across hybrid environments spanning legacy Windows, Linux, and Kubernetes-based infrastructure, including deep-dive root-cause analysis on complex, multi-tier system defects. Respond to customer inquiries via email and phone promptly and professionally. Host online troubleshooting and investigation sessions on customer production environments running on legacy Windows and Linux servers as well as Kubernetes-orchestrated infrastructure. Collect and document all necessary problem details, logs, and diagnostic data pulled from legacy Windows/Linux hosts and Kubernetes cluster telemetry alike to drive effective, evidence-based resolution. Successfully reproduce customer-reported issues in controlled test environments spanning legacy Windows/Linux systems and containerized Kubernetes platforms for root-cause analysis. Develop custom utilities, workarounds, and new solutions to resolve critical issues and improve product functionality across both legacy on-premises infrastructure and modern containerized platforms. Implement fixes for defects identified during troubleshooting or reported by customers and validate fixes through automated test suites prior to release. Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Azure DevOps) to automate build, test, and deployment of application code, hotfixes, and service packs across legacy Windows/Linux servers and Kubernetes environments. Deploy, configure, and manage containerized workloads on AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), including Helm chart management, namespace configuration, pod autoscaling, and zero-downtime rolling deployments. Administer and maintain legacy Windows Server and Linux infrastructure supporting existing production workloads, including patching, hardening, and performance tuning, while supporting migration of applicable workloads to Kubernetes. Monitor production system health, performance, and capacity across legacy Windows/Linux servers and Kubernetes clusters using observability tooling (e.g., AWS CloudWatch, Prometheus/Grafana, or Datadog) and proactively identify and remediate anomalies before they impact customers. Assist Product and Development teams with performance analysis, functional testing, and validation during release cycles (service packs, hotfixes, etc.), including automated regression testing within CI/CD pipelines. Partner with Product Implementation and Development teams to address complex issues and ensure smooth, well-orchestrated product delivery. Collaborate virtually with other Product Operations staff to ensure seamless teamwork and knowledge sharing across distributed teams. Provide mentorship and technical guidance to Product Support and Product Operations teams, including on legacy Windows/Linux administration, containerization, automation, and deployment pipeline practices. You’ll work on cloud architecture, security posture, and developer experience across a regulated financial services environment — and help support fellow engineers so we can grow without compromising reliability or compliance. Lendistry: Who We Are We’re proud to be the nation’s largest minority-led, tech-savvy lender for small businesses and commercial real estate. As a certified Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) and Community Development Entity (CDE), our mission is all about creating economic opportunities and fueling growth for small business owners and their communities. Join us as we pave the way with innovative financing and financial education! What You’ll Be Doing Collaboration & Mentorship Work as a hands-on individual contributor engineer on the Platform Engineering & Operations team, without formal people-management responsibilities. Help mentor junior engineers on the team, sharing knowledge as they grow their skills. Provide input and feedback on the technical roadmap for infrastructure and platform engineering. Cloud Architecture & Infrastructure Support cloud architecture and account management across development, staging, and production environments for a regulated lending platform. Help implement and maintain infrastructure-as-code and GitOps practices across infrastructure operations. Support container orchestration across multiple deployable services and cloud accounts. Security, Identity & Compliance Support identity management, account-level security posture, secrets management, and KMS key practices. Assist security and compliance teams with audits and vendor/security assessments for a regulated financial services platform. Developer Experience & CI/CD Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines across multiple repositories, from build through environment-gated production deployments. Support developer experience and internal tooling improvements for engineering teams. Reliability & Incident Management Participate in on-call and incident-response practices, including postmortems, for a platform where downtime directly impacts loan funding and servicing. AI-Native Platform Engineering Explore and help integrate AI-assisted engineering tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) into infrastructure workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and internal tooling. Support the adoption of AI-driven observability practices — anomaly detection, predictive alerting, and AI-assisted root-cause analysis — layered on top of existing monitoring stacks. Help support the infrastructure needs of ML/AI-driven product features (e.g., underwriting and fraud models), including model serving, inference monitoring, and compute scaling for AI workloads. Contribute to self-service internal tooling and golden paths that make it easier for engineers to ship safely. Your Areas of Knowledge and Expertise Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related discipline, or equivalent experience. 4+ years of experience engineering highly available, enterprise-grade software and platform applications. 2+ years of hands-on experience in platform engineering across various cloud computing models. 2+ years of hands-on experience with Kubernetes, container orchestration, Docker, and cloud-native applications. Substantial hands-on experience with public cloud platform services such as AWS, Azure, and GCP. Hands-on coding experience in at least two programming languages (Java, JavaScript, Python, Go, or .NET/C#). Experience with cloud-native application patterns and tools, microservices architectures, and application migrations to any cloud platform. Working understanding of infrastructure, virtualization, containers, networking, storage, and monitoring and logging/analytics tools (e.g., Splunk). Experience with application performance management tools (Splunk, AppDynamics, New Relic, Dynatrace, etc.). Experience with continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) tools and processes (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Ansible). Experience with developer tools and open-source technologies. Working familiarity with MLOps/LLMOps concepts and the infrastructure needs of AI/ML workloads (GPU or accelerator provisioning, model serving, inference cost and latency management). Hands-on use of AI coding assistants and developer tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) in real engineering workflows. Familiarity with policy-as-code (e.g., OPA, Kyverno) and software supply chain security practices (SBOM generation, artifact signing/provenance) as applied to CI/CD pipelines. Preferred Expertise 2+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), with hands-on experience in AWS production environments. Experience supporting cloud platforms aligned with the AWS Well-Architected Framework, with an interest in security, reliability, operational excellence, performance efficiency, and cost optimization. Hands-on experience with AWS core services, including VPC, EC2, IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, S3, networking, security services, and container orchestration platforms such as Amazon EKS or ECS. Experience working with infrastructure as code (IaC) using Terraform, AWS CDK, or AWS CloudFormation. Experience supporting CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions or Jenkins. Experience with cloud operations, including platform administration, production support, capacity planning, patching, and maintenance for AWS environments. Experience working with monitoring, logging, alerting, and observability tools such as Amazon CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana, and New Relic to support platform health, performance, and availability. Ability to participate as a technical escalation point during production incidents, supporting incident response, root cause analysis (RCA), and post-incident reviews. Familiarity with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles, including service reliability, SLAs/SLOs, incident management, change management, and operational readiness. Understanding of cloud cost optimization strategies, including resource right-sizing, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, storage lifecycle policies, and automation to improve operational efficiency and reduce cloud spend. Experience supporting DevSecOps practices, including automated security scanning, policy validation, compliance checks, secrets management, and vulnerability remediation within CI/CD pipelines. Good troubleshooting, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, security, operations, and platform teams. Interest in mentoring junior engineers and contributing to cloud engineering best practices is a plus. Interest in AI model governance and model-risk considerations (explainability, monitoring for drift/bias) in the context of AI-assisted decisioning within a regulated financial services environment. new_matches.title: Senior Technical Support Engineer
new_matches.description: Role Overview As a Senior Technical & Customer Support Engineer, you will handle advanced customer inquiries, providing in-depth troubleshooting for our Linux-based malware protection solutions. You will own support interactions end-to-end from triage to resolution or escalation, ensuring a seamless deployment process for the Monarx agent across various hosting environments. Key Responsibilities Triage and respond. Handle support requests across our Helpdesk, shared Teams/Slack channels and email, meeting our SLA response windows and keeping customers informed while issues are open. Get customers deployed. Guide customers through installing and rolling out the Monarx agent across their fleet, and work with them to fit the deployment to their environment: control panel, provisioning and configuration management tooling, OS and PHP mix, container or virtualization model, and whatever custom automation they've built. Stay with a rollout until it's working at their scale, not just on the first server. Troubleshoot the agent. Diagnose agent and provisioning issues: repository setup, package installation, OS and agent version mismatches, connectivity. Using diagnostic commands, configuration review, and log analysis. Gather complete intake. Collect the environment details required to reproduce and diagnose an issue (OS and version, agent version, hosting control panel, relevant logs, affected paths) before escalating, so engineering starts with a full picture instead of a thread of follow-up questions. Escalate well. Route complex or security-sensitive incidents to engineering and product with a clear written summary of what was observed, what was tried, and what's needed. Pulling in senior staff when the situation calls for it. Own our AI support tooling. Take ownership of the AI agent in Intercom. Curate the content and knowledge sources it draws on, review its conversations for wrong or incomplete answers, tune when it should resolve versus hand off to a human, and steadily expand the range of questions it can handle on its own. Own the knowledge base. Maintain and improve support documentation, help center articles, and internal runbooks. Written both for customers and to be machine-readable enough that the AI answers from them accurately. Close the feedback loop. Track ticket trends and AI deflection and escalation rates, identify recurring root causes and content gaps, and flag them to the product team as candidates for a real fix. Who we're looking for Required Direct experience at or with a web hosting provider. Deployment, provisioning, fleet management, or support Exposure to configuration management and automation tooling (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt) or container and virtualization platforms (Docker, LXC, KVM) Comfort with Linux command-line troubleshooting. Navigating a filesystem, package managers (yum/dnf, apt), services, and reading logs to find the relevant signal Clear, precise written communication, especially the ability to explain a technical issue to a customer without oversimplifying or overwhelming them Sound judgment about prioritization, and a good instinct for when to resolve independently versus when to escalate Comfort working directly with customers on issues that are urgent, ambiguous, or both Experience writing and maintaining support documentation or a customer-facing knowledge base Interest in using AI support tooling as a real part of the job, and the judgment to tell a good automated answer from a confidently wrong one Genuine interest in how hosting companies operate, deploy, and manage servers at scale. We'll teach you what you don't already know, but the curiosity has to be there Nice to have Hands-on experience with Intercom, particularly its AI agent / Fin, or a comparable AI-driven support platform Working understanding of security concepts: malware behavior, detection logic, false positives and false negatives Scripting ability (bash, Python) for pulling diagnostics together Experience with a ticketing or support platform and with SLA-driven workflows Support coverage and on-call Our customers run production infrastructure across multiple time zones, so support availability matters. We're location agnostic for this role, with a slight preference for Europe. Core coverage: Monday–Friday business hours in your local time zone Participation in a shared after-hours rotation for security-sensitive and production-impacting incidents Escalation path to senior engineering is available at all times; you are never expected to solve a critical incident alone What We Offer Competitive salary with equity opportunities. Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision. Flexible PTO policy. Remote working environment

new_matches.title: Product Installation Engineer - Innovation_Delivery_Transformation
new_matches.description: The Team ConvergeCONSUMER ™ is a product-driven business that combines differentiated consumer insights with robust prediction and optimization capabilities to help consumer-focused businesses improve decision-making and deliver personalized experiences to drive growth, consumer loyalty, and profitability. We operate with the speed and agility of a startup within the world's largest professional services firm. We drive value for our clients by optimizing decisions and actions at a level of granularity only made possible with today's data and technology. ConvergeCONSUMER's suite of solutions helps consumer-facing businesses prosper in a world being re-shaped by convergence, where the lines between industries, competitors and collaborators, consumers and suppliers, and even human and artificial intelligence have blurred. Our approach for addressing this complexity is simple: we combine Deloitte's next-generation technology platforms with decades of experience in the consumer sector and a deep understanding of its unique issues and challenges to drive profitability and future growth for our clients. Position Summary Cloud Engineering & Deployment, Expert Services Are you a hands-on cloud engineer who thrives on turning complex deployments into smooth, repeatable rollouts? As a Product Installation Engineer with ConvergeCONSUMER, you'll bring our suite of AI-driven products to life inside the cloud environments of some of the world's most influential consumer businesses. If you enjoy solving real infrastructure problems under real client conditions, we'd like to talk with you. Recruiting for this role ends on 9/30/2026. Work you'll do As the Product Installation Engineer within Expert Services, you will be responsible for installing one of a suite of applications, all following the same pattern of containerized applications with a React front end and Python business logic, into clients' cloud environments or on-premises data centers. This role requires hands-on expertise in instantiating and managing containerized applications, with a strong focus on cloud engineering, infrastructure provisioning, observability, and traceability. Key Responsibilities: Install and deploy containerized applications into clients' cloud environments or data centers. Manage and maintain containerized applications to ensure optimal performance and reliability. Collaborate with cloud engineering and security organizations to ensure infrastructure is provisioned correctly. Test the basic functionality of cloud applications to declare them open for business. Adapt logging and monitoring hooks to integrate with clients' native operations, ensuring observability and traceability. Assist the developer team with remote debugging and troubleshooting issues. Automate deployment processes to achieve quick time to value for clients. Communicate technical requirements for cloud deployments clearly, including concepts like access groups, roles, permissions, and networking. Work with common cloud infrastructure components such as VPCs, managed services, and storage solutions. Manage data ingress and egress requirements, including moving large datasets within cloud contexts and across cloud instances. Ensure compliance with clients' security and operational standards. Stay up-to-date with the latest industry trends, tools, and technologies to continuously improve deployment practices and processes. The successful candidate would possess these skills: Hands-on approach to deploying and managing containerized applications in complex, client-facing cloud environments, with a strong bias toward reliability, repeatability, and quick time to value. Deep familiarity with cloud infrastructure fundamentals, including VPCs, managed services, storage solutions, access groups, roles, and permissions, and the ability to communicate these concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical client stakeholders. Strong infrastructure-as-code instincts, with the ability to automate and standardize deployment processes across varied client environments and data centers. Comfort operating at the intersection of cloud engineering and security, collaborating with client infrastructure and security organizations to ensure compliant, correctly provisioned deployments. Proven ability to adapt observability and monitoring frameworks to client-native operations, ensuring traceability and operational continuity post-deployment. Methodical troubleshooting approach with experience supporting remote debugging and resolving complex deployment issues in collaboration with developer teams. Fluency in data ingress and egress requirements, including the ability to move and manage large datasets within and across cloud environments. Curiosity for emerging cloud technologies and deployment practices, with a continuous improvement mindset that keeps pace with a rapidly evolving infrastructure landscape. Qualifications Required: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. 5+ years of professional cloud engineering experience. Ability to travel 25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve. Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future. The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $116,200-$229,100. You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

new_matches.title: Principal Database Engineer – SQL Server & AI Data Infrastructure
new_matches.description: Principal Database Engineer – SQL Server & AI Data Infrastructure The Opportunity WEX is looking for a highly experienced Database Engineer to help modernize and scale critical data platforms while supporting the next generation of AI-enabled applications. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who brings deep expertise in SQL Server and T-SQL, combined with the ability to solve complex database performance, scalability, and modernization challenges at enterprise scale. You will work across large, business-critical data environments, partnering closely with application engineering, SRE, operations, and architecture teams. The role is highly technical and execution-oriented—you will be expected to independently identify problems, drive solutions, and take ownership from design through implementation and production. The team is also applying modern AI capabilities to database engineering, including AI-assisted development, automation, semantic search, embeddings, and vector-based data infrastructure. What You'll Do Database Engineering & Modernization Design, develop, optimize, and modernize large-scale SQL Server databases and data platforms. Analyze and refactor complex T-SQL, stored procedures, functions, and database logic. Identify and resolve database performance bottlenecks through execution-plan analysis, indexing, query optimization, and database tuning. Drive schema improvements and database modernization initiatives that improve scalability, maintainability, and reliability. Develop migration strategies and automation that maintain data integrity and minimize disruption to business-critical systems. Implement and improve data replication and synchronization patterns across transactional and analytical environments. Apply event-driven database patterns such as Change Data Capture (CDC), outbox patterns, and event publishing. Enterprise-Scale Data Platforms Engineer solutions for large, high-volume databases supporting critical business applications and partners. Work with databases containing terabytes of data and complex data relationships. Develop data pipelines and integration patterns across SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and cloud data services. Support both OLTP and OLAP environments and optimize data movement between systems. Apply strong understanding of database internals, including indexing, locking, transactions, isolation levels, concurrency, and query optimization. AI-Enabled Database Engineering Use modern AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar tools to accelerate development, analysis, debugging, and modernization. Explore and implement AI-powered approaches for analyzing stored procedures, documenting schemas, and automating database engineering workflows. Contribute to AI-native data infrastructure, including embedding pipelines, vector databases, semantic search, and retrieval systems. Develop data and retrieval capabilities that support AI applications and agentic workflows. Evaluate emerging AI tools and determine where they can improve engineering productivity and data platform capabilities. Technical Leadership & Ownership Independently lead complex database engineering initiatives from problem definition through production implementation. Serve as a technical resource for complex database and performance challenges. Partner effectively with application engineering, SRE, operations, architecture, and AI/ML teams. Provide technical guidance through code reviews, design discussions, and engineering standards. Mentor other engineers and contribute to the development of database engineering practices. Take ownership of outcomes rather than simply completing assigned tasks. Production & Problem Solving Participate in resolving high-impact production issues involving critical database systems. Diagnose complex problems using logs, database metrics, CPU/memory utilization, execution plans, and other observability data. Quickly determine root cause, coordinate with the appropriate technical teams, and drive issues through resolution. Balance immediate incident resolution with longer-term improvements that prevent recurrence. What You'll Bring Required Experience 15+ years of experience in database engineering, data platform engineering, software engineering, or a related technical discipline. Deep hands-on experience with Microsoft SQL Server and T-SQL, including complex stored procedures, query optimization, execution-plan analysis, indexing, and performance tuning. Demonstrated experience modernizing or refactoring legacy database systems, not simply maintaining existing environments. Experience working with large-scale, business-critical databases and high-volume data environments. Strong programming skills in Python, C#, or a similar language for automation, tooling, and data processing. Experience with data pipelines, ETL/ELT, data integration, batch processing, and/or event-driven architectures. Strong understanding of database internals, transaction management, concurrency, locking, and performance optimization. Experience working across engineering teams and independently driving complex technical initiatives. AI & Modern Data Technologies Experience using AI coding assistants such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Augment, or similar tools. Familiarity with embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, or RAG concepts. Experience with or willingness to build AI-enabled data tooling and automation. Exposure to technologies such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, AWS data services, or similar platforms. Cloud & Engineering Practices Experience with infrastructure-as-code such as Terraform, ARM/Bicep, or similar technologies. Experience with CI/CD, source control, database migrations, schema versioning, and deployment automation. Experience with event streaming technologies such as Kafka is a plus. Familiarity with NoSQL and document databases is a plus. Preferred Experience Experience in payments, financial services, healthcare, benefits, or other highly regulated environments.
